Under universal p_G=essential, each Q_epsilon is compact and hence finite rank; B=norm-lim BQ_epsilon compact. Any kernel unit x gives a rank-one projection R_x with p_G(R_x)=1 but essential norm zero, contradiction. Conversely, if B is compact injective, Q_epsilon finite rank and P_epsilon=I-Q_epsilon strongly tends to zero; two-sided near-norming estimates show p_G(T)=lim||TP_epsilon||. Finite-rank TQ_epsilon gives the lower bound essential≤limit, and compact K times P_epsilon tends to zero in norm, giving the upper bound. Injective compact operator has separable dense image, so only separable H possible; diagonal compact positive B and G=(I-B)^1/2 supply examples. All real/complex infinite-dimensional H, all bounded T; equality for only one T is not asserted.
